title: Lina Attalah: Egypt court fines journalist Lina Attalah and orders Mada Masr's closure
description: The editor-in-chief of the independent Egyptian news outlet Mada Masr was detained for several hours after a court convicted her of managing an unlice
body: The editor-in-chief of the independent Egyptian news outlet Mada Masr was detained for several hours after a court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website and ordered its closure, her lawyers say.Mada Masr said Lina Attalah was released once it paid the fine of 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100) also handed down to her by the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court. It was the maximum possible penalty for the charge, which she had rejected.Amnesty International said the verdict represented "a crushing blow to press freedom".It comes only weeks after six journalists working for the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh were charged with belonging to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.Egypt is among the top jailers of journalists globally, with 25 currently behind bars, according to the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ).President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi has overseen what human rights groups say is an unprecedented crackdown on dissent since he led the military's overthrow of his predecessor, Muslim Brotherhood leader Mohammed Morsi, in 2013.Tens of thousands of people have been detained, mainly Brotherhood officials and supporters but also leading secular and liberal activists, media workers and academics.The CPJ said Mada Masr, which was founded in 2013, was a vital source of critical reporting in Egypt and that it had long faced pressure from authorities over its journalism.The site had repeatedly sought an operating licence from the Supreme Media Regulatory Council (SMRC) since a new media law was passed in 2018, but that its applications were either rejected or left unanswered, the media watchdog added.Amnesty International said Lina Attalah had also faced "years of harassment and intimidation", including six criminal investigations over Mada Masr's reporting.Last week, prosecutors summoned her for questioning over allegations of publishing "false news" and operating a website without a licence.Mada Masr's lawyer said the investigation included a recent report that the website had published about a wave of protests in prisons across the country, as well as a letter from the SMRC regarding its legal status.Attalah was released on bail and later referred to trial before the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court on the charge of operating a website without a licence.During Tuesday's hearing, Judge Mohammed Mubarak ordered the courtroom to be cleared of everyone except Attalah, her eight-person defence team, and Hossam Bahgat, head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), an independent human rights group.Bahgat told AFP news agency that security personnel then filed in before the judge announced that the court was denying several procedural requests made by the defence and appointing its own lawyer for Attalah."In a move that astonished all those present, the judge recorded in the official court minutes that the court had appointed a lawyer from the Lawyers' Syndicate to represent the defence," he said. "Lina herself spoke up to object to this lawyer being appointed to represent her, which the judge refused to record in the court minutes."In an even more shocking turn, the judge proceeded to dictate motions on behalf of this lawyer - who had not uttered a single word - and entered them into the official record," he added.The judge then announced the fine for Attalah and ordered Mada Masr's closure "amid shouts and protests from the defence", before she was detained, according to Bahgat.On Tuesday evening, Mada Masr said it had paid the full fine to the court and that Attalah was released after several hours in custody."During the release procedures, Attalah learned of a one-year prison sentence issued against her in absentia in 2024, on charges of publishing false news and managing an unlicensed website," it added."Her lawyers took steps to challenge the ruling, with a hearing in a retrial of the case scheduled for 11 November."Amnesty International warned that the court's verdict marked "a dark day for independent journalism" in Egypt and demanded that it be overturned."This draconian ruling is the culmination of years of relentless harassment and unjust proceedings designed to shut down one of the country's last remaining independent media voices," said the group's senior director for regional impact, Yasmine Ahmed."Lina Attalah should never have been prosecuted for exercising her right to freedom of expression and doing her journalistic job."CPJ Regional Director Sara Qudah said: "If Egypt can put in custody one of its most respected editors and shut down her newsroom, no independent journalist in the country is safe. Attalah must be released immediately, and Mada Masr must be allowed to keep reporting."

schema.headline: Lina Attalah: Egypt court fines journalist Lina Attalah and orders Mada Masr's closure

title: Ghanaian twins and US woman plead guilty to romance scams
description: Twin brothers from Ghana and an American woman have pleaded guilty to being part of an international criminal network that defrauded people on dating
body: Twin brothers from Ghana and an American woman have pleaded guilty to being part of an international criminal network that defrauded people on dating sites and social media.The group targeted elderly people in the US and Europe, using fake identities to lure their victims into believing they were in a romantic relationship, before persuading them to transfer large sums of money into bank accounts in Ghana.The 22-year-old twins, Jamal and Kamal Abubakari, and 53-year-old Amanda Joy Opoku-Boachie from Hawaii face up to 20 years in jail and will be sentenced next year. Between July 2024 - April 2026, the victims collectively lost $9m (£6.7m).While many of them were from Ohio - where the charges were brought - other victims were located in 24 other US states, as well as Germany and Austria. As part of the plea, the Abubakaris and Opoku-Boachie agreed to forfeit pieces of jewellery which investigators seized during their arrest, including luxury watches, rings, chains and earrings.

schema.headline: Ghanaian twins and US woman plead guilty to romance scams

title: Jordan says 'terrorists' killed in Syria in retaliatory strike over church attack
description: In response to the strike, Syria said it had closed a border crossing with Jordan."The decision includes the complete suspension of passenger and comm
body: In response to the strike, Syria said it had closed a border crossing with Jordan."The decision includes the complete suspension of passenger and commercial traffic in both directions, to ensure the safety of travellers and workers at the crossing," Syrian authorities said in a statement carried by state media.It added that it had "opened direct channels of communication" with Jordanian officials and had launched "comprehensive investigations to establish the full circumstances of the targeting".Nassib is the only passenger and commercial border crossing between Jordan and Syria.Earlier on Monday, senior government security officials said Jordanian security forces had arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law over the church attack. The Public Security Directorate (PSD) said the unnamed "terrorists" were found hiding in an abandoned house in Karak before dawn.Jordan's Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya told state-affiliated TV the attackers were all Jordanians and "had been holed up in a building in one of the villages near the site of the attack".

schema.headline: Jordan says 'terrorists' killed in Syria in retaliatory strike over church attack

title: Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking case
description: One by one, they spoke of the psychological trauma they endured after the Alexander brothers raped them, and their desire for the shame they had felt
body: One by one, they spoke of the psychological trauma they endured after the Alexander brothers raped them, and their desire for the shame they had felt to instead fall on the defendants.Many asked the judge to impose the maximum sentence of life in prison for each brother.Maya Miller told the court that after Tal Alexander raped her in 2014, she lost all sense of safety. "I carry a quiet funeral within me for the person I might've become if this never happened to me," she said.Another victim, using the pseudoym Isa Brooks, said after being raped by Tal and Alon Alexander when she was 16, she lost the ability to trust herself."I had no idea the danger I was in till it was too late," she said.Another woman said when she planned to come forward about being raped, Tal Alexander threatened her, saying he knew where her sister worked.Prosecutor Elizabeth Espinosa said the brothers deserved the maximum punishment for their crimes, saying facts "paint a truly devastating picture"."For years, they honed their methods of luring women with the promise of luxury," she said, adding that they were "completely unmoved by the path of suffering they left behind them."During the women's speeches, the three Alexander brothers showed little emotion. They stared ahead or conferred with their lawyers, who said they advised their clients not to look at the victims so it couldn't be misconstrued.Attorneys for the brothers pushed for sentences of 15 years, arguing that they had become devoted fathers whose families would suffer in their absence.The three men all addressed the court, continuing to profess their innocence."We had a work-hard, play-hard mentality," Tal Alexander said, adding he saw how his behavior "hurt people's feelings".But their statements did not assuage Caproni, who chastised them for refusing to admit their crimes."How can someone who never acknowledged the wrongs they did be rehabilitated?" she asked.At the end of the hearing, she sentenced them each to 30 years in prison for certain crimes. She also sentenced each to 20 years in prison for additional crimes, but said the men would serve the sentences concurrently.During the five-week trial, 11 women - several said they were minors at the time of the assaults - testified that the brothers gave them gifts and flew them places including Aspen and the Bahamas where they fed them drugs before raping them. Prosecutors said the brothers' pattern of abusive behaviour began in high school, though the trial involved crimes starting in 2008. They said the three slipped drugs into women's drinks, and "physically restrained and held down their victims during the rapes and sexual assaults and ignored screams and explicit requests to stop".Lawyers for the brothers argued the sex was consensual and that they were womanisers, but not abusers. Two of the brothers, Tal and Oren, became wealthy selling luxury properties in New York and Miami. They worked for American real estate giant Douglas Elliman, with clients including Lindsay Lohan, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West. In 2022, they founded their own New York-based firm called Official. Alon worked at the family's private security firm, Kent Security.As they heard their sentences, the brothers stared straight ahead.

schema.headline: Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking case

title: Nanotyrannus: Dinosaur skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction
description: The mounted skeleton of a newly-identified dinosaur once mistaken for a young Tyrannosaurus rex has sold at auction for a colossal $47.3m (£35.5m).Nic
body: The mounted skeleton of a newly-identified dinosaur once mistaken for a young Tyrannosaurus rex has sold at auction for a colossal $47.3m (£35.5m).Nicknamed Jodi, the roughly 10-foot-tall (3m) skeleton was auctioned by Sotheby's in New York. The sale comes a year after researchers confirmed that the skeleton belongs to a distinct genus.The Late Cretaceous carnivore was expected to fetch at least $9m when it went under the hammer on Tuesday. The auction comes after Sotheby's sold a Tyrannosaurus rex, dubbed Gus, for a record $50.1m in July.The sale has reignited debate in the scientific community over whether dinosaur remains should be sold privately or displayed publicly.Sotheby's described Jodi as an "excellent exhibition-ready" skeleton with about 191 fossil-bone elements and a "beautifully preserved, virtually complete skull".The auction house added that the Nanotyrannus is "one of only three such skeletons known to science". The specimen is the first to come to market since the existence of the genus was confirmed by US researchers last October, Sotheby's said.The identify of the buyer, who won after a thrilling 12 minutes of auction bidding between six interested parties, has not been disclosed.It becomes the second-most valuable dinosaur fossil ever sold, behind Gus. The third-most valuable was a Stegosaurus named Apex, which was sold by Sotheby's in July 2024 for $44.6m.Megan Jacobs, a palaeontologist at the University of Portsmouth, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Tuesday that Nanotyrannus "was for a very long time believed to be sort of a teenager of T. rex"."But it's a lot smaller and its a lot more gracile. So it's very sort-of sleek, slender, [with] blade-like teeth for slicing through meat," Jacobs said.Tyrannosaurus rex and Nanotyrannus lived alongside one another during the same geological period approximately 67 million years ago.Jodi was initially exhibited as a juvenile T. rex at London's Frieze Masters international art fair in October 2023, before the Nanotyrannus genus was classified.The skeleton was discovered in the US state of Montana by rancher Jodi Pierson on her land in the Hell Creek Formation, a heavily studied geological site. It was later excavated by commercial palaeontologist Clayton Phipps.Phipps also discovered the famous "Dueling Dinosaurs" fossil. That specimen, which shows the remains of a Nanotyrannus and Triceratops apparently in combat, was found eight miles (13km) away from Jodi in 2006.The "Dueling Dinosaurs" discovery became crucial to the research published by Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli that classified Nanotyrannus as separate from T. rex. Their paper ended decades of debate over whether the dinosaurs were distinct from one another.The auction of Jodi comes as some scientists warn that auctions could herald a new era in fossil collecting by the ultra-rich.Researchers told the BBC after the sale of Gus that such remains should be exhibited in public spaces where they can be more freely studied.Prof Steve Brusatte, a palaeontologist at the University of Edinburgh and consultant on the Jurassic Park films, told BBC World Service's What in the World programme in July that the T. rex's auction was "concerning"."I don't know of any museum or university that can afford a price tag like that," he said. "Imagine if the Mona Lisa was just owned by a super-wealthy person and it wasn't on display and people couldn't see it, couldn't enjoy it."He said at the time that he hoped such a sale didn't become a trend, adding it could adversely affect scientific research and public education.Responding to Tuesday's auction, Brusatte called it "harrowing" that Jodi could disappear from public view. "We've really just found out that Nanotyrannus is real, and now one of the best skeletons is about to be sold to the highest bidder, and it's harrowing to think it could disappear into the vaults of a collector rather than displayed on a museum where it can wow and inspire kids and families and the public at large," he told the BBC.But Jacobs told the Today programme on Tuesday there were two sides to the debate, and that a lot of time, effort and money went into excavating the specimens."I don't begrudge the people involved for wanting to sell it for such a large amount of money," she said. "Although its a scary prospect, actually a lot of them have ended up in the public eye... these things without a doubt will end end up in a museum at some point."

schema.headline: Nanotyrannus: Dinosaur skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

title: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds
description: The investigating committee found that the raid on the miners had been conducted without an approved operational order, proper planning or consultatio
body: The investigating committee found that the raid on the miners had been conducted without an approved operational order, proper planning or consultation with the Mining Marshals Unit.It said that 50 detainees had been held in a cell measuring about 20 sq m, with no running water or functioning toilet, and inadequate food, drinking water and airflow.Adults and minors were detained together, and some detainees were held beyond lawful detention periods. Officers reportedly ignored repeated calls for help, despite a medical worker having raised concerns about the conditions."Detainees repeatedly banged on cell doors and walls, shouted for assistance and pleaded for water," said the head of the investigating team, Jonathan Kure."These distress calls were heard by officers assigned to nearby duties... but were not acted upon."Kure said the detention conditions amounted to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment."The tragedy demonstrates the consequences of systemic disregard for detention standards, supervisory responsibilities and the welfare of persons in custody," he added.The investigating committee also recommended compensation of 30m naira (£16,683; $22,285) for each of the bereaved families and 10m naira for each survivor.

schema.headline: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds

title: Super Bowl 2027: Jay-Z to perform at half-time show
description: Rapper Jay-Z will perform at the Super Bowl half-time show in February, the NFL has announced.Jay-Z's company Roc Nation has produced the half-time sh
body: Rapper Jay-Z will perform at the Super Bowl half-time show in February, the NFL has announced.Jay-Z's company Roc Nation has produced the half-time show since 2019, and he plays a key role in selecting each year's performer but he has not performed before at the NFL championship game."Anticipation as to who Jay-Z might have guest star at halftime for the big game will now kick off," the NFL said in a statement. "Of course, his wife, Beyoncé, will be atop the list." Next year's Super Bowl LXI will take place on 14 February near Los Angeles.The hip-hop star will follow in the footsteps of other recent half-time performers including Bad Bunny, Kendrick Lamar, Usher, Rihanna and The Weeknd.The musical performance draws global attention while the sport is watched by tens of millions of people in the US.Kendrick Lamar's 2025 performance was the most watched Super Bowl half-time show in history and won the Emmy award for outstanding music direction.The announcement was made after Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, performed two shows last weekend at the Los Angeles stadium where the Super Bowl will be played.The LA shows were part of a tour to celebrate the 30th anniversary of his debut album Reasonable Doubt."From 'Reasonable Doubt' to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey," said Jay-Z."Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true."NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said he "couldn't be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring"."When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him," Goodell said.The star's accolades include being the first rapper inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame, 25 Grammy awards and being inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2021.

schema.headline: Super Bowl 2027: Jay-Z to perform at half-time show

title: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
description: Image source, Reuters/HandoutImage caption, The people of Oleshky have had no electricity for years and no access to food or waterByPaul KirbyEurope d
body: Image source, Reuters/HandoutImage caption, The people of Oleshky have had no electricity for years and no access to food or waterByPaul KirbyEurope digital editorOlga Malchevska and Dan Johnsonin KyivUpdated 1 hour agoA ceasefire that began with the aim of getting food and medicine to the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has been extended across the wider southern region of Kherson, according to sources.Several thousand residents are trapped in the city with no access to food, water and electricity. On one side is the Dnipro river, while Russian forces are on the other and all the roads out are too dangerous.However, no breaches of the truce that began early on Tuesday have so far been reported.US First Lady Melania Trump, who helped broker the ceasefire along with Pope Leo XIV, said on Tuesday that the area involved had been expanded to provide "safe passage" for humanitarian convoys.Figure caption, What we know about Ukraine-Russia truce in Oleshky, brokered by Melania TrumpThat was later corroborated by the press secretary to Ukraine's public ombudsman, and by Oleksandr Tolokonnikov, deputy head of Kherson, who said Russian shelling had stopped both in Kherson city, which is in Ukrainian hands, and the wider region.Under the deal, the ceasefire will be followed by deliveries of humanitarian aid to Oleshky and then evacuations, planned for Friday, for anyone wishing to leave.An estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people remain in Oleshky itself and a few thousand more in surrounding areas.Many residents have resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive, telling the BBC they are suffering extreme hunger and want to leave.Both sides said the ceasefire was being observed. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said everything was proceeding "according to plan", and paid tribute to US mediation and in particular representatives of Melania Trump.Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said if the ceasefire produced results, it could "pave the way for other steps in the peace process".A key official in President Volodymyr Zelensky's parliamentary party, David Arakhamia, said it would continue until 22:59 Ukrainian time on Sunday 1 November, and described the truce as the "largest de-escalation since 2022".Before the war Oleshky was home to 24,000 people, but it was seized by Russia during the first days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022.No shops are open, and the city has had no electricity, gas or water since the Kakhovka Dam was blown up in 2023, flooding the area and killing many people in Oleshky itself.Conditions have become so desperate that not only is getting supplies into the city extremely difficult, but escaping is too risky because the routes out of Oleshky have been mined and subject to drone attack.One woman told the BBC she had stepped on a landmine and was currently in hospital where she had undergone two operations: "I don't know how long I will have to spend there," she said, worried about not being able to join the evacuation.Pope Leo appealed earlier this month to Russia's President Vladimir Putin to allow food and medical aid into Oleshky as well as a safe evacuation, and urged his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky to co-operate with Moscow over a ceasefire.Then the White House said last week that Melania Trump had secured a ceasefire.On Tuesday, the US first lady said on X that the area covered by the ceasefire "has expanded beyond Oleshky, within the Kherson region, to provide safe passage for the humanitarian convoys".Image source, Ksenia ArkhipovaImage caption, These residents were able to get out of Oleshky in spring this yearThe current truce is supposed to enable roads to be cleared of mines for supplies to get into the city possibly on Thursday, and for residents to have safe passage out in an evacuation planned for Friday.Russia's defence ministry said units from the army's Dnepr group had been conducting "engineering reconnaissance" and clearing main access roads into the village of "explosive and booby-trap devices".Many details on the evacuation plans are unclear, and residents are wary of trusting officials with their names and addresses. However, a local volunteer told the BBC that about 500 people had already expressed interest by Tuesday afternoon.Vladimir Saldo, the Russian-installed head of occupied areas of Kherson, said temporary accommodation had been prepared in the region itself as well as Russian-annexed Crimea and across the Russian border in the Rostov, Krasnodar and Stavropol regions.Saldo told Russian media that most Oleshky residents wanted to leave the city and stay in Russia, although his account has not been corroborated on the ground.Image source, Ombudsman Dmytro LubinetsImage caption, Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since 2022 and its people are now trappedIt is hard to make contact with people there as communication is patchy and many are reluctant to speak of the situation in fear of reprisals from the Russians.Those residents or relatives who have spoken to the BBC have expressed fears that Russia may not allow them to return to Ukraine, or might examine their phones and online activity for signs of Ukrainian support, which could put them in danger.Ukraine's military general staff urged people not to trust unverified reports or spread rumours about "the routes, time and place of the movement of people and humanitarian convoys".Zelensky has warned that routes out of Oleshky that are demined by Russia will ensure that those civilians leaving Oleshky will "head towards Russia and stay there". He said some residents would get to Ukrainian-controlled territory "one way or another", and that ideally anyone trapped would be able to reach their destination and evacuate to Ukraine.One resident called Serhii, who fled Oleshky through minefields around three weeks ago, said he had eventually returned to Ukraine via Russia and Belarus. He called for a route across the River Dnipro that avoided Russian-occupied territory, saying "you simply cannot trust the Russian Federation".However, bridges across the River Dnipro have been destroyed and sources say the riverbank is also mined and dangerous, so crossing into Ukrainian-controlled territory appears impossible.Across the river, in Kherson city, no explosions have been heard and no drone-related injuries reported since 03:00 (01:00 GMT) on Tuesday and cars and pedestrians have been moving freely, according to local reports."Judging from the fact that more people are walking around, it feels a bit calmer," Galina Kyrychenko, a resident in the city, told public broadcaster Suspilne.Additional reporting by Anastasiia Levchenko in Kyiv.

schema.headline: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say

title: How 'anti-superstar' Harry Kane defied doubters to achieve Ballon d'Or greatness
description: Harry Kane has taken the scenic route to the Ballon d'Or - a road littered with doubts and diversions, but one that eventually led to the ultimate des
body: Harry Kane has taken the scenic route to the Ballon d'Or - a road littered with doubts and diversions, but one that eventually led to the ultimate destination: being crowned as the world's best player.The 33-year-old's glory at the London Palladium on Monday is fitting reward for an exemplary career that has seen records fall at his feet for England, Tottenham Hotspur and Bayern Munich.Kane is England's top goalscorer with 91 goals. He has 125 England caps, joint-highest with Peter Shilton. He is Spurs' record scorer with 280 goals in 435 appearances. He scored a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for Bayern Munich and England during the 2025–26 season.This is the Kane of recent vintage, the world-class striker and complete footballer who beat Real Madrid and France striker Kylian Mbappe, as well as Spain's teenage Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal, to the sport's biggest personal honour.Kane's humility has seen him described as an 'anti-superstar' and his achievement has been commended both inside and outside the football world.One post on social media from Kane as he celebrated the greatest moment of his career said it all: "Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise."And yet, Kane's journey was not always smooth. It was one that started with loan moves around the lower divisions with Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City before he developed into a great for club and country.The same Kane sat on the bench on loan at Leicester City – alongside future England team-mate Jamie Vardy – when the Foxes lost a dramatic Championship play-off at Watford in May 2013.Kane went through hard schools and hard times away from his more familiar environment at Spurs, joining Orient on loan as a 17-year-old in January 2011, playing 18 games with nine starts and scoring five goals.He joined Millwall in similar circumstances a year later, with some behind the scenes at Spurs fearing the traditionally hostile atmosphere at the New Den might intimidate the teenager, but he acquitted himself well, scoring nine goals in 24 starts.Former Spurs manager Tim Sherwood said: "I used to watch Harry a lot at Millwall and it was an intimidating atmosphere. I remember overhearing one of our scouts come and talk to Harry Redknapp - who was Spurs manager at the time - and say: 'We need to get Harry Kane out of Millwall, it's no good for him there'."I went straight in and said: 'This is the perfect atmosphere for him'."Kane made his Spurs debut in August 2012 before a spell at Norwich City, where he failed to score in three starts and suffered a serious foot injury.It was an unhappy time but Chris Hughton, the former Spurs defender who was manager at Carrow Road, said: "What I saw in him was a desire to do well. Did I see him having the mobility and flexibility he has in his game now? Probably not. He was a very good finisher. He would stay out after training for half an hour every day, left foot, right foot."Next stop was Leicester City between February and May 2013, when he made five starts and scored two goals, a stint best remembered for that dramatic Championship play-off game when Troy Deeney scored for Watford to send them to Wembley seconds after Anthony Knockaert's penalty was saved by Manuel Almunia.Kane was not even selected in Leicester's starting line-up, only being sent on after 61 minutes. And who was alongside him on the bench? Vardy, who later won the Premier league with the Foxes and played alongside Kane for England.He later admitted this was a time of self-doubt, saying: "That was probably the time in my career where it was the hardest - I was 19 and I was thinking, 'If I can't play for Norwich or for Leicester, even in the Championship, then how I am going to get back and play for Tottenham?'"It is testimony to Kane's strength of character, even as a youngster, that he not only returned to Spurs but left for Bayern Munich in August 2023 as one of their greatest ever players.Even at Spurs, Kane's superb record always carried the qualification that he never won a trophy, a stick used to unfairly beat a player whose remarkable consistency and approach marked him down as the consummate professional.Kane has put that right spectacularly at Bayern, winning the Bundesliga twice, the move propelling him to the level of global superstar, giving him the profile and platform to win the Ballon d'Or - the first English player to win the trophy since Michael Owen in 2001 and the fifth overall.Former England midfielder Danny Murphy told BBC Sport recently: "He's a born goalscorer. He's a super professional. He's technically brilliant. He's been an absolute credit to himself and his family in the way he's conducted himself and the longevity he's had in his career."There is still that one space on his roll of honour, namely success with England after losses in two Euros finals and two World Cup semi-final defeats, but who would bet against Kane being fit and motivated enough to have one last crack at Euro 2028 in the UK and Ireland.Kane is now at the peak of his powers and fitness, not just a goalscoring machine but the complete player capable of dropping deep into midfield to play the sort of breathtaking defence splitting pass exemplified by Alphonso Davies' goal against Arsenal in the recent Champions League game.One of Kane's illustrious predecessors in England's number nine shirt, Alan Shearer, told BBC Radio 5 Live: "It was so well deserved because he hasn't had things all his own way. He's had to go round it the hard way. He had to start off the hard way by someone telling him, 'You're not quite good enough, you're going to have to work a lot harder to get to where you want to'."He did that. He went out on loan and worked harder than anyone else. He's got to the very, very top and now he's the best player in the world and that's what dedication does for you. It's a message to everyone."Harry said it in his speech - that if you're told you're not good enough, then go and try again and work harder. He did that and look where he is now. He's been scoring goals at a phenomenal rate for so many years now and he deserved it."Shearer added: "I think the best thing for me is how humble Harry is. Footballers are like movie stars nowadays. You see them walking down the red carpet and some of them are in sunglasses when it's pitch black and eight o'clock at night. Harry is just normal, as normal as they come."Once the celebrations die down, it will be back to business for the humble superstar, with Bayern playing Magdeburg in the German DFB Pokal second round on Wednesday before the big home fixture against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday evening.Kane's career has not been without its obstacles but he remains as focused as ever to conquer whatever is placed in front of him by Bayern Munich and England.

schema.headline: How 'anti-superstar' Harry Kane defied doubters to achieve Ballon d'Or greatness

title: Norway and Finland hold rare call with Putin to discuss ending war
description: The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.Finland
body: The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said the aim of the call had been to "convey messages directly regarding future negotiations" towards peace. An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Stubb said. Neither side suggested the needle had been moved on ending the war, which began when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Although the Finnish leader said the conversation with Putin had been "frank and substantive," Støre added that there were "big differences in views" with Putin.Several European leaders have recently shown willingness to engage with Russia directly, but both Stubb and Støre pointed out their initiative was taken in their capacity as neighbours of Russia, rather than on behalf of Europe as a whole."We've not set out to speak on behalf of anyone other than ourselves," Støre said. Stubb added the call had been prepared in consultation with Ukraine and the US following a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, the Nordic leaders and US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo last week.The first trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks since the start of the year are tentatively planned for early November in Abu Dhabi.Zelensky later confirmed Stubb and Støre debriefed him after the call and said he was grateful for their "active support", while his Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the call had been "the right approach".Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the 90-minute call - held from Helsinki - to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.Støre added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered. Putin also reaffirmed to the Nordic leaders what he views as the "root causes" of the conflict - his frequent shorthand for Ukraine's desire to exist as a sovereign state. "A fair long-term peace settlement is possible only if Russia's legal interests are taken into account fully and unconditionally", Putin said.All three parties reportedly agreed to continue their direct phone communication.There was no official EU reaction to the talks. The dialogue had not been coordinated with other European leaders, the Danish and Swedish prime ministers said. "I think Europe should stick together rather than going solo," commented Sweden's Ulf Kristersson. Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Stubb had informed him that Europe's position on the upcoming talks in the United Arab Emirates was "moderately optimistic".Relations between the US and Ukraine and its European allies have soured since US President Donald Trump agreed to lift some sanctions from Russia, allowing Moscow to export oil to the America. As the Trump administration's position on Russia has softened, several European leaders have said Europe should be trying to re-establish direct contacts with the Kremlin.Stubb and Støre are the first European leaders to contact Putin since French President Emmanuel Macron's conversation with him in July 2025.Soon after, Putin visited Alaska for a summit with Trump, and from then on Europeans were further sidelined from Ukraine peace talks. Moscow regularly mocks European leaders and accuses the EU of prolonging the war by supplying Ukraine with weapons. But last weekend, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said having a European negotiator at the peace talks table would be "good". And although he said Moscow did not view Finland and Norway as speaking on behalf of Europe, on Tuesday Peskov conceded that Stubb and Støre's talks with Putin had been "very constructive and practical talks with the leaders of two key neighbouring states."

schema.headline: Norway and Finland hold rare call with Putin to discuss ending war

title: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China
description: Kylian Mbappé has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese
body: Kylian Mbappé has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese brands. Mbappé had reportedly told French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." He then laughs as the clip cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a "dictator" because of his huge influence in football. "My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world,"  Mbappé said in a statement."I apologise to everyone my words have upset."Spain's La Liga also apologised, saying it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappé's recent comments have caused among Chinese fans".The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead.A few people came out in support of him on Chinese social media, but that is a rare response given China's tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics.Few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands were so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like Mbappé.  The original video is not available on the show's YouTube channel, and it's unclear when the interview hosted by Real Madrid's Aurélien Tchouaméni first aired. In clips that have been circulating online, Mbappé does not identify Mao by name. He says he "uses [the meme] with friends all the time".The furore appeared to kick off on Monday night after Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments in a statement, saying they were "inappropriate" and "hurt the feelings of Chinese people".Screengrabs of the clip and meme have since spread quickly on Chinese social media, with people echoing this sentiment and even calling for a boycott of both the French striker and his club, Real Madrid.But some have blurred the meme itself as well as the part of the comment they found offensive, when Mbappe refers to "a Chinese dictator". Dongqiudi said in its statement that it was "unable to translate" his comments because they were "offensive to China and the Chinese people".  Many people are therefore also wondering what exactly Mbappe said and have responded to the angry posts and comments with questions, wanting to know more.  Chinese fans have been criticising Mbappé – who is popular in China and has huge brand endorsements – of "profiting from the Chinese market yet making remarks that offend the Chinese public"."International public figures, in particular, should show greater respect and sensitivity, as national sentiment must never be taken lightly," reads another  comment on Weibo.As the anger online grew louder, Chinese brands began to cut ties, although they did not explicitly refer to the video.  The country's largest dairy producer, Mengniu, said it "firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people".Drinks giant Dongpeng issued a similar statement: "Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments."According to state-owned newspaper The Global Times, state broadcaster CCTV's news apps will not feature content related to the French striker. CCTV will also stop showing La Liga matches, Chinese media reported on Tuesday. Real Madrid is one of 20 clubs that play in the Spanish football league and is the most decorated team with 36 league titles.China's foreign ministry has also weighed in, with spokesperson Lin Jian saying: "We have noted the relevant reports. Words and deeds that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with opposition from all sectors of Chinese society."It's unclear when the Mbappé meme involving Mao began but his nickname, "the dictator", has made the striker the subject of many memes and jokes online. Mbappé is widely regarded as one of the best footballers in the world and has wielded significant influence at the clubs he has played for. His extraordinary speed, goalscoring ability and worldwide popularity have made him a global icon, attracting millions of fans, major sponsorship deals and media attention, with his influence extending into fashion, culture and business.In 2024, he sued a French influencer and kebab shop owner for using his name in the description of one of the shop's sandwiches, leading to more jokes about the nickname. France teammate Ousmane Dembele jumped on the trend during the 2026 World Cup, calling Mbappé Mobut – a reference to Mobutu Sese Seko, the dictator who ruled the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, for three decades.In an interview with France Football in September, Mbappé acknowledged the light-heartedness behind many of these memes, but said they "sometimes reveal a lack of political and human awareness among people"."There's a side that's a bit less funny, because we know the damage people like that have caused throughout history," he said."Being compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions upon millions of people miserable... I don't think I've done that in my life."Additional reporting by Fan Wang and Osmond Chia

schema.headline: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China

title: Sudan war: West warns of famine risk
description: The US and 30 other Western states have warned of an "alarming deterioration" in food security in Sudan, urging the warring sides in the civil war to
body: The US and 30 other Western states have warned of an "alarming deterioration" in food security in Sudan, urging the warring sides in the civil war to remove obstacles to humanitarian aid to prevent famine.In a joint statement, the signatories said conflict was the main driver of Sudan's hunger crisis, damaging critical infrastructure and disrupting food production."There is very little to survive on," Yusuf Roble, regional director for Islamic Relief East Africa, told BBC Newsday, describing how people returning to Omdurman were finding their homes destroyed or looted.The war, which began in April 2023, has displaced 14 million people.The statement, external was signed by EU states, the UK, Canada, Switzerland and Norway, as well as the US, where it was published by the state department on Monday after first appearing on the European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations website.It estimates that 19.5 million people or 41% of Sudan's population are experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity, including five million facing emergency levels of hunger."I met a mother of seven children who doesn't really know the whereabouts of her husband for the last three and a half years and he was the breadwinner, the sole breadwinner for the family," Roble said.While the war in Sudan has led to what the World Health Organization has described as the world's worst humanitarian crisis, Roble said only 40% of Sudan's 2026 humanitarian needs plan had been funded as of September."Their meals come from the community kitchen, which doesn't really even have very long-term support because of funding cuts," Roble added.The joint statement warns that "the number of children suffering from severe acute malnutrition could exceed the projected 825,000" without immediate action.The crisis is being exacerbated by what the signatories describe as systematic obstruction of aid and the effects of El Niño, which has reduced rainfall and increased drought across more than half of Sudan."The parties to the conflict bear primary responsibility for alleviating the suffering of the Sudanese people," the statement says, urging them to lift all impediments to humanitarian assistance and allow full, safe, rapid and unimpeded access.In June, the UN-backed Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, a measure of the severity and magnitude of food crises, estimated that 5.1 million people in Sudan faced severe hunger. The civil war in Sudan began in April 2023 following a power struggle between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.

schema.headline: Sudan war: West warns of famine risk

title: Lula's comeback in Brazil dents Trump's ambitions for Latin America
description: If that sounds muddled, it is because the relationship between the two men is not straightforward. Trump did not explicitly endorse Lula's rival Flávi
body: If that sounds muddled, it is because the relationship between the two men is not straightforward. Trump did not explicitly endorse Lula's rival Flávio Bolsonaro, who refused to recognise the result. But Trump was a close ally of Flávio's father, the former President Jair Bolsonaro.When I spoke to Lula at his residence about a year ago, relations had hit rock bottom. He told me he had "no relationship" with Trump, that they had never spoken, and that he had no intention of picking up the phone. Trump had recently imposed punitive tariffs on Brazil, largely as a political response to Jair Bolsonaro's coup trial, which the US president called a "witch-hunt".Rather than tiptoeing around Trump, as some US allies did, Lula fought back – and it paid off. He made fiery speeches invoking Brazilian sovereignty, attacked US interference in the judicial process, and took to wearing a blue cap reading "Brazil belongs to Brazilians". His approval ratings jumped. He accused the Bolsonaro family, who had lobbied for the tariffs, of being unpatriotic – a blow to a political right that so often claims patriotism as its terrain. Even some in the agricultural lobby, typically strong Bolsonaro supporters but reliant on US trade, thought Lula had a point.The US eventually backed down and reduced the tariffs, although they have since risen again. Relations then improved. The two men spoke at the United Nations and later met in the Oval Office, where Trump called the talks "very good" and Lula said he left "very satisfied". Another indication, perhaps, that Trump likes a strong leader.So why might Trump be unhappy with the result?Latin America has swung to the right, with Ecuador, Chile, Colombia, Argentina and Peru all electing presidents closely aligned with the Trump administration. Trump has sought to use these allies to establish US dominance in the Western Hemisphere, a strategy he has dubbed the "Donroe Doctrine".Christopher Sabatini, senior fellow for Latin America at Chatham House, notes that Trump thought Brazil would be the "10th and biggest prize" after Flávio Bolsonaro won the first round. Brazil is Latin America's largest economy, and the younger Bolsonaro was expected to join Trump's "Shield of Americas" coalition against narco-trafficking. Brazil also holds the world's second-largest reserves of rare earth minerals after China, and the US had been eyeing preferential access.The relationship has thawed, but with four more years ahead for Lula, several issues could reignite tensions.Brazil accused the US earlier this year of trying to cast doubt on its electoral system and denied visas to two state department officials planning to visit. The US called this "baseless" and revoked the Brazilian ambassador's visa in response. If Trump keeps calling this result "rigged", further diplomatic fallout is likely.Lula has also vehemently opposed US military action in the region, from the seizure of Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela to the bombing of alleged drug-trafficking vessels. He lambasted Washington for designating Brazil's two major gangs as terrorist organisations after lobbying from Flávio Bolsonaro, and warned of attacks on Brazilian sovereignty.It is a sensitive subject for a political left that remembers the region's brutal 20th Century dictatorships, many backed by the CIA in the name of stopping communism.Then there is US tech. Lula's campaign accused Meta of favouring Flávio Bolsonaro. Meta denied this but admitted moderation issues and technical errors had wrongly removed some posts or limited their reach. Lula's supporters responded by sharing his messages through a 10-million-strong WhatsApp group to bypass the algorithms.Separately, the Trump administration is unhappy with Pix, Brazil's instant payment system, which has boosted the economy, but which the US sees as taking business from Visa and Mastercard.The relationship has exposed political divisions. In the campaign, Bolsonaro supporters waved US flags at their rallies and, in one case, an inflatable saying "Trump Nuke Brazil", while Lula and his supporters accused Flávio Bolsonaro of protecting US interests over Brazil's.Still, tensions can be overstated.The US remains Brazil's second-biggest trading partner after China, and for now the two leaders get on. Whether that lasts will depend on how far the US tries to intervene in Brazilian affairs, and how bullish Lula is in response.

schema.headline: Lula's comeback in Brazil dents Trump's ambitions for Latin America

title: Ballon d'Or ceremony raises case of French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes jailed in Algeria
description: The plight of French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes, who is serving a seven-year prison sentence in Algeria, was highlighted at the Ballon d'Or
body: The plight of French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes, who is serving a seven-year prison sentence in Algeria, was highlighted at the Ballon d'Or ceremony.Run by France Football magazine, the prestigious football awards were held in London where presenters Kate Scott and Thierry Henry dedicated the occasion to the 37-year-old reporter.On a large screen behind them, it stated that he had been in jail for one year, three months and 27 days and alongside his photo was the hashtag "#FreeGleize".He was arrested on a trip to Algeria where he had gone to report on a football club in Kabylie, a region where some people want self-determination. The authorities accused him of supporting terrorism."The Ballon d'Or France Football family would like to take this opportunity to dedicate this ceremony to Christophe Gleizes," said British broadcaster Scott and former Arsenal player and French striker Henry as the ceremony kicked off on Monday evening.The event, held in London for the first time in its 70-year history, saw England and Bayern Munich strike Harry Kane crowned the world's top footballer of the year and London's City's Spanish midfielder Alexia Putellas taking the female prize.Gleizes, who contributes to French magazines So Foot and Society, travelled to Algeria in May 2024 to report on Jeunesse Sportive de Kabylie (JSK), one of the country's best-known football clubs.It is based in Tizi Ouzou, about 100km (62 miles) east of the capital Algiers, in the mountainous Kabylie region, which is mainly home to the ethnic Amazigh people (historically known as Berbers).It is also the base of the Movement for the Self-Determination of Kabylie (MAK), which Algeria designated a terrorist organisation in 2021.Gleizes was accused of possessing publications deemed harmful to national security.The case centred on his contacts with a JSK official who was also associated with the MAK.Reporters Without Borders (RSF), which has campaigned for his release, says the exchanges took place in a journalistic context and that some contacts predated the outlawing of the group.During his appeal hearing last December, Gleizes acknowledged mistakes in his reporting and said he should have applied for a journalist visa rather than entering Algeria on a tourist visa."I beg your mercy so that I can be reunited with my family," he told the court.Prosecutors argued that he had not travelled to Algeria to carry out journalistic work, but to commit a hostile act.The Algerian authorities have yet to commented on the decision by the Ballon d'Or, which is organised by France Football magazine in partnership with European football governing body Uefa, to dedicate the ceremony to Gleizes.RSF has announced a solidarity football match for 11 November, marking Gleizes's 500th day in detention, as part of its campaign calling for his release.Former France internationals Robert Pirès and Vikash Dhorasoo, along with Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire, are among the first participants announced.Gleizes's case comes amid wider concerns over the prosecution and imprisonment of writers and other public figures in Algeria.Franco-Algerian writer Boualem Sansal was sentenced to five years in prison for undermining national security before receiving a pardon from President Abdelmadjid Tebboune following mediation by Germany's president in 2025.Gleizes's arrest also came during a period of heightened diplomatic tensions between France and Algeria, marked by the withdrawal of ambassadors and reciprocal expulsions of diplomats.Relations deteriorated further after France recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara in July 2024. Algeria supports the pro-independence Polisario Front, which seeks independence for the disputed territory.As relations began to improve in May, France's Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin visited Algiers and urged the Algerian authorities to allow Gleizes to reunite "not with France, but with his mother".He said that he believed President Tebboune would be receptive to the request.

schema.headline: Ballon d'Or ceremony raises case of French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes jailed in Algeria

title: Nigerian controversial Islamic cleric Yahaya Masussuka shot dead in Katsina state
description: A controversial Islamic cleric in Nigeria has been murdered outside his home in the northern state of Katsina.Two assailants arrived on a motorcycle a
body: A controversial Islamic cleric in Nigeria has been murdered outside his home in the northern state of Katsina.Two assailants arrived on a motorcycle and shot Yahaya Masussuka in the town of Dutsin-Ma as he was saying goodbye to visitors on Monday evening, sources told the BBC.The 47-year-old preacher and one of his guests, who was also shot, were rushed to hospital but both were pronounced dead by the attending doctor, police said.It is not clear why Masussuka was targeted, but the cleric had received death threats on social media where he posted videos in which he rejected some elements of mainstream Islam, including what happens to people after their death.It is widely believed in Islam that a person's soul will be questioned in the grave by two angels. If they answer correctly, their soul sleeps peacefully until the day of judgement - if not it will be tormented.This understanding comes from what is known as the Hadith, a collection of texts believed to be the spoken words and actions of the Prophet Muhammad.This serves as a key source of Islamic knowledge to help interpret the Quran, the central religious text of Islam.But Masussuka based his teachings mainly on what was in Islam's holy book, questioned some of the hadiths - and did not believe that the dead were reawakened and questioned.He was once jailed for nine months because he teased some respected scholars over their belief in this hadith and other teachings.Masussuka, who had two wives and seven children, began preaching at the age of 13 in Quranic schools.He later attended Al-Azhar University in Egypt and later went to Oman for further studies.At his home, he had a studio where he would record videos of his teachings for broadcast on social media for his followers.The cleric was also outspoken about violent extremism, radicalisation and openly advocated for interfaith dialogue and peaceful coexistence between Muslims and Christians, who make up nearly equal parts of Nigeria's population.Thousands of Christians and Muslims have been killed in ethnic and religious violence here over the past 25 years.For Masussuka's efforts, Nigeria's Network for Good Governance and Transparency honoured him with a Peace Ambassador Award last year.Six other prominent Muslim preachers have been murdered over the last two decades in northern Nigeria - several targeted by Boko Haram for criticising the jihadist group that began its insurgency in 2009.Founded in north-eastern Nigeria, it opposes Western culture, education, the secular government - and its political goal is the creation of an Islamic state.Additional reporting by BBC Pidgin

schema.headline: Nigerian controversial Islamic cleric Yahaya Masussuka shot dead in Katsina state
